newsitem.title: BRAZIL: BRAZIL'S LEFT-WING WORKERS PARTY LOSES GOVERNOR.
newsitem.headline: BRAZIL'S LEFT-WING WORKERS PARTY LOSES GOVERNOR.

text.p: Brazil's left-wing Workers Party (PT), the main opposition to the government of Fernando Henrique Cardoso, has lost one of its most senior positions of power following the resignation from the party of Espirito Santo state governor Vitor Buaiz.

Buaiz, a founding member of the PT and considered one of its most centrist figures, said he was leaving the party after coming under fire from "revolutionary" hardliners opposed to his plans to cut jobs in the Espirito Santo government.
"When there is sectarianism, everyone loses -- party, government and society," the governor said in a letter distributed Monday after a meeting with party leaders in Sao Paulo.

The departure of Buaiz leaves the PT with just one governor, Cristovam Buarque in the Federal District. It also exposes deep rifts within the party just as it prepares for the 1998 presidential, state governorship and congressional elections.
"The level of sectarianism and internal conflict within the PT puts its survival at risk," party president Jose Dirceu told daily newspaper O Globo. "The party must learn from this episode."
But other PT luminaries said they were not sorry to see Buaiz go. "He had to go because he did not follow the party's program," said Congressman Milton Temer, a leader of the PT's hard left.
